title: Emerging Technology Weekly Briefing
description: Quantum and post-quantum cryptography, robotics and autonomy, advanced compute, and space-enabled tech.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 3–13. New: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 12 that the Space Development Agency awarded SpaceX $9.9 million to study connecting Plaser laser terminals with missile-tracking satellites. No new post-quantum standard or Army quantum award dated Nov. 12–13 was found. The compute subsection is empty. The Nov. 6 report that those laser waveforms do not match remains.

items.headline: DeepMind says Gemini Robotics 2.5 kitted parts at 96 percent on a Mercedes line
items.summary: Google DeepMind said Nov. 10 that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is its most capable vision-language-action model and is rolling out to robotics partners. DeepMind said a proof of concept with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz used Apollo 2 humanoids to pick and pack automotive parts on production lines in Kecskemét, Hungary, and Sindelfingen, Germany, at a 96 percent success rate. DeepMind said the model was evaluated across more than 200 tasks and, compared with previous baselines, raised success rates by 30 to 100 percent depending on the task while finishing 20 to 30 percent faster. DeepMind said inference-time guidance raised safe task completion by 33 percent around obstacles and 43 percent around nearby people.

items.headline: Navy and Marine Corps will demo TRUAS cargo drones in Huntsville in early 2027
items.summary: Defense News reported Nov. 3 that the U.S. Marine Corps and Navy will hold a technology demonstration from Jan. 25 to Feb. 5, 2027, in Huntsville, Alabama, for Increment II of the Marine Corps Tactical Resupply Unmanned Aircraft System. The outlet said the Navy's Air Warfare Program Management Office is sponsoring the event, and that contractors will perform up to five flights and show ground setup. Defense News said the first required flight carries a 100-pound payload up to 40 nautical miles and returns without refueling, and the second carries at least 150 pounds out to 10 nautical miles. It said the aircraft must have a speed of at least 50 knots per hour, stay at or below 1,000 feet during those flights, and launch and recover without a catapult or arresting gear.

items.headline: Space Development Agency pays SpaceX $9.9 million to study Plaser links to missile trackers
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 12 that the Space Development Agency awarded SpaceX a $9.9 million contract, with options worth up to nearly $12.7 million, to study how the company's Plaser laser terminals can connect with the agency's missile-tracking satellites. An SDA spokesperson said the study covers hardware, software, and connectivity for moving data from the Tracking Layer to the Plasers, and that the work runs through Oct. 7, 2027, including a risk-reduction study and representative hardware. Breaking Defense said the optical terminals on the Space Data Network Backbone and on Space Development Agency and Space Systems Command missile-warning satellites use different waveforms. The spokesperson called the study a first step, with several hardware and software paths still open.

items.headline: Office of Strategic Capital commits a $150 million conditional loan to Rocket Lab
items.summary: The Department of War said Nov. 9 that the Office of Strategic Capital signed a $150 million conditional loan commitment with Rocket Lab USA to increase the flight rate of its reusable Neutron rocket after first launch. The release says the loan would support faster vehicle delivery and processing, more maritime vessels and equipment for Neutron recovery and transport, manufacturing upgrades for composite structures and engines, and infrastructure to cut turnaround time. It says Neutron is designed to deliver about 13,000 kilograms to low Earth orbit for constellation deployment and national security payloads. The commitment is not a financial close: Rocket Lab must still meet financial, legal, technical, investment, and due-diligence requirements, and Under Secretary for Research and Engineering Emil Michael endorsed the transaction.

items.headline: Breaking Defense: Space Force laser terminals cannot talk across the Golden Dome data backbone
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 6 that SpaceX's optical terminals on the Space Data Network Backbone, which the company calls Plasers, cannot directly exchange data with the optical terminals on Space Development Agency and Space Systems Command missile-warning satellites. An SDA official confirmed to Breaking Defense that the optical waveform on SDA's Transport Layer and Tracking Layer satellites is not directly compatible with the Plaser waveform. Breaking Defense said sources described a proposed set of 12 or 13 translator satellites, called Space Exchange Points, at $12 million to $14 million each, and said the wider fix could reach $1 billion. It said SpaceX won a $2.29 billion contract in May for the backbone, and that a Space Systems Command spokesperson declined to comment on compatibility with the Plaser.

items.headline: Office of Strategic Capital commits a $150 million conditional loan to LeoLabs
items.summary: The Department of War said Nov. 4 that the Office of Strategic Capital signed a $150 million conditional loan commitment with LeoLabs for space domain awareness and space traffic management. The release says the loan is matched dollar-for-dollar with co-investment, for a $300 million capital infusion, and that the financing would scale multi-mission phased-array radars, including mobile Scout units. It says the commitment is not a financial close: LeoLabs must still meet financial, legal, technical, investment, and due-diligence requirements. Under Secretary for Research and Engineering Emil Michael said the financing is meant to help the United States and allies control the data used for decision advantage in orbit.
